Align a raster to a template

Source: R/align.R
align_raster.Rd

Puts a raster onto a template raster's grid: the template's CRS, extent, resolution and cells, such as an AOI raster onto the national 1 km template so national data can be extracted for it, or a merged mosaic back onto the national template. The input can be any one-layer raster, on a smaller, shifted, finer or coarser grid, or in another CRS.

Usage

align_raster(
  x,
  template,
  filename = NULL,
  resample = "near",
  datatype = NULL,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

The raster to align: a SpatRaster with one layer and a CRS, or a path to a raster file with one layer.

template

The reference raster: a SpatRaster with one layer and a CRS, or a path to a raster file. Only its grid is used (CRS, extent, resolution), not its values.

filename

The file to write the aligned raster to: a single string, or NULL (the default). With NULL, a file input (a path, or a SpatRaster read from a file and not changed since) is written to <input>_align.tif beside it, as wtw-data-prep2's align_pu() did: for example pu_1km.tif gives pu_1km_align.tif. An in-memory input with NULL is not written, and the result stays in memory.

resample

The resampling method, passed to terra::project() as method: one of "near" (nearest neighbour, the default, as align_pu() used), "bilinear", "cubic", "cubicspline", "lanczos", "sum", "min", "q1", "median", "q3", "max", "average", "mode" or "rms". Use "near" or "mode" for categories and cell numbers, which must not be averaged.

datatype

The data type of the written file, one of terra's types: "INT1U", "INT2U", "INT2S", "INT4U", "INT4S", "INT8U", "INT8S", "FLT4S" or "FLT8S". NULL (the default) uses the data type of the file x was read from, as gdalwarp does; an in-memory x has none, so datatype is then required to write it. Ignored when nothing is written.

overwrite

A single logical: TRUE (the default) replaces an existing filename; FALSE stops with an error if it exists.

Value

A SpatRaster with one layer, named as x's layer, on the template's grid: x's values resampled to the template's cells, NA outside x. When written, it is read back from filename, which holds a GeoTIFF (or the format of filename's extension) in datatype.

Method

  • Warp: terra::project() with the template as the target grid and method = resample (GDAL's warper). The result has the template's CRS, extent and resolution exactly, so its cells line up with the template's. terra::project() is used even when x is already in the template's CRS, so the result always carries the template's CRS. When reprojecting, cell centres are transformed exactly, as gdalwarp does with et = 0, not with gdalwarp's default approximate transformer (ADR 0007).

  • Cells: each template cell takes its value from x at the cell's centre ("near"), or from the cells of x around the centre or under the cell for the other methods. Raster, not vector, operations: no areas are computed.

  • Outside x: template cells outside x's extent are NA, also when x has no NoData value. The warp runs without writing (to memory, or to a temporary file for large rasters) and the result is then written with terra::writeRaster(), so cells outside x are never filled with 0.

  • Writing: in datatype. For an integer type the values are first rounded to the nearest whole number, halves away from zero (terra::round()), because GDAL truncates decimals when it writes them as integers; with "near" on an integer input nothing changes. NA is written as terra's NoData value for the type (for example 255 for "INT1U"). A result kept in memory is not rounded.

Method choices are recorded in ADR 0007 and ADR 0010. Compared with wtw-data-prep2's align_pu() (gdalwarp), the cells and values are the same, except that cells outside an input with no NoData value are NA rather than 0, a few edge cells can differ when reprojecting (gdalwarp uses an approximate transformation by default), and the stored CRS and grid are the template's exactly.

If x's extent, reprojected to the template's CRS, does not overlap the template's extent, the function stops with an error.

See also

rasterize_aoi() with crop = FALSE puts an AOI polygon on the template's full grid directly.

Other raster: polygonize_raster(), write_rasters()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")

# An AOI raster of 1s cropped to the AOI, written as a file
pu <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches", value = 1)
pu_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "pu.tif")
terra::writeRaster(pu, pu_file, datatype = "INT1U", overwrite = TRUE)

# Aligned to the template's full grid, written beside it as pu_align.tif
x <- align_raster(pu_file, template)
x
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1000000, 1010000, 600000, 610000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source      : pu_align.tif
#> name        : aoi
#> min value   :   1
#> max value   :   1
basename(terra::sources(x))
#> [1] "pu_align.tif"

# An in-memory raster stays in memory unless a filename is given
align_raster(pu, template)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1000000, 1010000, 600000, 610000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> varname     : template
#> name        : aoi
#> min value   :   1
#> max value   :   1

# A raster in another CRS is reprojected onto the template's grid
utm <- terra::project(
  terra::rast(template), "EPSG:32616",
  method = "near", res = 1000
)
align_raster(utm, template)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 10, 10, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 1000, 1000  (x, y)
#> extent      : 1000000, 1010000, 600000, 610000  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#> source(s)   : memory
#> varname     : template
#> name        : index
#> min value   :     3
#> max value   :   100
